novelty.justification: The claim proposes the new mechanistic relationship that “distant, low-resource languages need MORE layers to finish computing a concept” and that a fixed-depth model therefore “runs out of layers,” distinguishing unfinished computation from missing knowledge through a per-item required-depth estimand. Searches around “multilingual transformer required depth low-resource language,” “cross-lingual errors fixed depth truncation,” “language-specific adaptive computation,” and “late-layer looping multilingual LLM” found adjacent work on multilingual layer-wise decoding (Indic-TunedLens, 2026) and elastic or recurrent depth (Inner Thinking Transformer, 2025; Change of Thought, 2025), but not the specific prediction that language distance and resource level induce a causal depth deficit responsible for cross-lingual errors. Moving from those strands to this claim requires a new core relationship rather than merely changing the studied language or renaming adaptive depth, although it remains within established probing and test-time-compute frameworks rather than introducing a new paradigm.
